source: rtconfirm-p6-t13 side effect of the P6-RT-07-01 fix (fixout/confirm-t13.json)
claim: Since the P6-RT-07-01 fix, a link state of T13 (166 of the 167 Atlas links, /embed/satake/ links, M9 instance links) shows the real-form names in the Data and Catalogue panels as the plain markup of t13/names.ts (Unicode fraktur, no MathML) until the reader's first paint, tau, picker, example, catalogue entry, panel or back; actions that change neither the pair nor the panel (root, theta stages, composite moves, undo, redo, reset) never load them.
expected: SPEC 7.5 A-12 (mathematics rendered with MathML available to assistive technology) and SPEC 7.6 (a tool alone within 90 kB of JavaScript before the first interaction, link states included, as the adopted link-size test asserts). decisions/P6-A3.md: 'the first view is always the typeset one'.
observed: Link state names plain until an action; the whole names chunk satakeNames.*.js weighs 5230 B gzip, and /tools/satake/ measures 87.2 kB, so loading it during hydration puts link states at 92.4 kB.
proposedFix: Split the typeset names so that a link fetches only what it shows (for example one small chunk or JSON per board, imported by board name), loaded during hydration for a link state, keeping every link state within 90 kB before interaction (the adopted link-size test and the RT-07 sweep over the 167 Atlas links) and the default route unchanged. If no design meets both A-12 and 7.6, mark needs-decision with the measured options.

source: rtconfirm-p6-t13 side effect of the P6-RT-10-05 fix
claim: The decoration's paint buttons now carry data-board="numbers" with data-value 1 (black) or 0 (white). SPEC 4.0 defines data-value as the value shown and data-board as the game's board; the decoration draws no numeral and plays neither game, so its hooks tell a reader (and Challenge.svelte's valuesOf) that it is a numbers board holding 1 and 0.
expected: SPEC 4.0 Test hooks; 6.3 last bullet (the decoration is drawn on its own copy so that black and white never compete with the sign encoding).
observed: On M9 b10 the 'numbers' group reads [1:1 2:0 3:1 4:0 5:0]; with the restricted panel open (b7, b12) the 'populations' group interleaves the E6 game board and the A2 restricted board.
proposedFix: Treat the paint buttons as controls rather than node buttons (a data-control hook naming the label and the colour in data-colour, no data-node), keeping their keyboard behaviour (one tab stop, arrows, Home, End, Enter, Space), focus, announcements and every test, if 4.0 allows it; otherwise mark needs-decision with the options (a third data-board value logged as a change to 4.0). Note in the fragment what a Challenge of kind reach, distinct or mixed-signs on a T13 instance would read with the restricted panel open (none exists today).
